observer: Claude (Opus 5.5), 9 Nov 2026: the raw scan (1841 x 2349) blurred 3x3, whole with a 0.05 grid and two crops at 0.02; read for the structure's shape, not against a render
covers: the left wall's post at SL-3M with its bent run and flared gusset, the riveted rounded housing at the floor, and where the racks end
notes: session A (9A33BM2/BM3, not identified). The post is the left-side counterpart of g098-a's post d07; the shapes are similar but on opposite walls, and I cannot prove they are mirror images. Its catalogue name in the register is not clear, so new.post.rear_left is proposed; it may be frame.post_sl2m_sl3m.

details.what: the post's upper run: a vertical flat member carrying the plate of fuse data, a lit raised edge at its aft side
details.size_cue: about as wide as the fuse table's plate

details.what: the post's aft edge below the plate, a rough weld-like ridge bending down and aft
the post's forward edge, a dark gap down it from the plate, bending aft like the ridge, the post narrowing a little to the bend
the gusset at the post's foot: below the bend the sheet flares forward and outward into a wide triangular web, its forward edge running out to the white-panel column
details.size_cue: the web about as wide as the post at its foot
details.note: g098-a d10 is the same kind of flared foot on the other wall; which is bigger is not known

details.what: the flared web's surface: wrinkled, patched and stained, brown along the bend, looking like filled or brazed sheet
a round dark hole in the post near the keys, its rim rough; something oval inside
a rounded housing rising at the gusset's foot, grey-green and smooth, its top outline a low arch across the frame's bottom
details.size_cue: as wide in the image as about three of the white panels
details.note: not the round floor cover of g100-d (domed rivets here, flange bolts there; a different shape). It may be the left wheel-arch hump seen from above; I could not prove that from this frame

details.what: domed rivets along the housing's upper flange
the rack's bottom at left and the dark sill under it, set in from the post
a flat ledge of the left wall under the rack, in the distance, seen beyond the gauge sheet, with a notched bracket on it
the tall grey sheet leaning against the post, carrying the gauge at its corner, its lower corner cut, a lit edge up its near side
a dirty rough sheet or sacking pad on the floor by the sheet's foot
the white panel column's frame on the forward side of the post, a straight vertical edge where the post's web ends
